eventMetadata.context_description: **Strong high-pressure dominance and southerly flow are positioning Madrid for a peak near 39°C today.** Latest model runs and observational data show mostly clear skies, light winds, and dry air allowing efficient daytime heating, with afternoon temperatures climbing from morning lows around 22–24°C. Consensus across guidance supports a maximum of 38–39°C, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward 39°C at 72% implied probability and 40°C at 23.5%. This exceeds the 1991–2020 September 4 average high of roughly 29°C and approaches the 2016 record of 37°C. Minor model spread on exact timing of peak heating and urban heat-island effects introduce the modest probability mass on 40°C, while official AEMET station readings through the afternoon will resolve the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from Malaysia's meteorological agency project a maximum of 35°C for Kuala Lumpur on September 4 amid typical early-September equatorial conditions, with afternoon thunderstorms and haze potentially limiting peak heating. Multiple numerical models converge on 32–34°C highs, with slight differences arising from the timing and intensity of convective rain, cloud cover, and urban heat retention. High humidity near 80% and light variable winds reduce evaporative cooling while increasing apparent temperatures, but scattered showers—forecast with 30–65% probability—can suppress readings by 1–2°C if they develop before peak insolation. Trader consensus favoring 33–34°C reflects this narrow range of outcomes, where a delayed storm or clearer skies could tip the daily maximum either way before official station data finalize the result.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lemd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from GFS and ECMWF models place Madrid’s September 5 maximum in the 34–37 °C range, with afternoon peaks driven by southerly flow, light winds, and limited cloud cover that allows strong solar heating under high pressure. This distribution underpins the market’s tight clustering around 36–37 °C, while modest model spread on boundary-layer moisture and timing of peak insolation keeps 38 °C viable though less probable. Historical September 5 records near 37.4 °C provide context but do not override current dynamical guidance. Traders will watch the next 00z and 12z model cycles plus any AEMET updates for shifts in the thermal ridge before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models from Taiwan's Central Weather Administration and international sources indicate a highest temperature in Taipei on September 5 most likely in the 30–32°C range, with showers and variable cloud cover as the key moderating factors.** Persistent humidity near 70–90% and northwest winds around 5–11 km/h will limit full solar heating, while any afternoon clearing could push peaks toward 32°C or briefly higher. Historical September averages hover near 30°C, providing baseline context, yet current model runs show divergence based on exact rainfall timing and intensity—85–97% precipitation probability in some guidance keeps 33°C+ odds low at 15%. Traders appear to weigh official 26–32°C outlooks heavily against ensemble uncertainty, with resolution depending on verified maximum readings from local stations. Updated forecasts overnight will refine these probabilities ahead of final observations.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Kuala Lumpur Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=wmkk

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from sources including GFS and ECMWF points to a clear, high-pressure regime over Cape Town on September 5, with light to moderate southeasterly winds and minimal cloud cover supporting afternoon maxima near 21–23 °C. These conditions align with the market’s leading outcomes of 23 °C and 24 °C, reflecting typical early-spring climatology where oceanic moderation from the Benguela Current limits extremes despite strong insolation. No significant warm advection or subsidence anomalies have emerged in the latest runs, keeping probabilities for 25 °C or higher subdued. Traders will monitor the final overnight and morning updates from the South African Weather Service for any last adjustments to boundary-layer mixing or wind strength that could shift the peak by 1–2 °C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Persistent southwest monsoon flow and widespread convective activity driven by the Habagat are the dominant factors capping Manila’s daytime maximum near 28–30 °C on 5 September. Official PAGASA guidance and ensemble forecasts indicate thick cloud cover, frequent thunderstorms, and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds that reduce insolation while enhancing evaporative cooling and mixing. These conditions produce a narrow temperature distribution centered on 28–29 °C, aligning with the market’s near-even implied probabilities for those two outcomes and the lower odds assigned to 31 °C or higher. With rain likely throughout the daylight hours, any brief clearing could allow a brief spike toward 30 °C, but renewed convection is expected to keep readings from exceeding that threshold.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Benito Juárez International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 5 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mmmx

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts for Mexico City on September 5 point to a daily maximum near 24°C under mostly cloudy skies and scattered showers linked to nearby tropical waves and Cyclone Marie activity, which enhance cloud cover and limit daytime heating. Multiple model runs and historical September climatology, with typical highs of 23–25°C, reinforce this range, though timing of rainfall could allow brief spikes toward 26°C if convection holds off longer than expected. Trader positioning at 26°C (44.5%) or higher appears driven by uncertainty in precipitation timing and model spread rather than current observational trends or baseline seasonal data. Updated guidance from Mexican meteorological services and ensemble consensus will likely clarify resolution odds ahead of market close.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Recent forecasts from models including GFS and ECMWF point to daytime maxima of 29–31°C in Panama City on September 5, aligning with the market’s clustering around 30–32°C.** In the tropical wet season, high humidity, trade-wind patterns, and afternoon convection typically cap temperatures near the long-term September average of about 31°C, while scattered thunderstorms can suppress peaks through cloud cover and evaporative cooling. A developing El Niño event, with equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperatures well above average and >90% probability of persistence through late 2026, is expected to reduce regional rainfall and may allow slightly clearer intervals that favor the upper end of the range. Short-range model consensus and limited day-to-day variability keep the 32°C outcome as the modal outcome, though any increase in organized convection or earlier sea-breeze onset could shift realized highs downward. Updated NHC and local IMHPA guidance ahead of the date will provide the next key inputs for traders.
